$comment: Central component inventory and lock set. This file is the single source of truth for
every external component CloudBurrow builds on. Reproducible builds consume the
'verified' versions here; #31 maintains it and tests 'latest-candidate' sets in an
isolated lane. A mutable tag may be used for discovery, never as the release pin:
'digest' is what a reproducible artifact resolves.

project.$comment: CloudBurrow's own licence, which test/repo's TestLicence checks against LICENSE. Every component below keeps its own licence; the guard refuses GPL, LGPL and AGPL code in third_party/ and in the modules linked into the CLI.

project.earlierReleases: v0.1.0 to v0.5.0: first published under Apache-2.0; their CloudBurrow code is also available under MIT

mode.verified: The pinned set below. Used by all ordinary, release and offline builds.
mode.latestCandidate: Discovered by #31, tested in isolation, never used for release artifacts until promoted here.

patches: CloudBurrow's: decodes the base64 of each BYTES value a streamed row, a load or a query's rows carries before it is bound, where the engine stored the base64 text as the bytes (#1065, #1075)
goccy/googlesqlite#76 (open upstream, by its author, unchanged): casts ARRAY elements and nested STRUCT fields, so a RECORD inside a REPEATED RECORD reads back after a stream or load (#900)

CloudBurrow's: keeps each table function's outer handle, which owns go-googlesql's finalizer, referenced for the catalog's life, so a garbage collection no longer frees a table function the catalog still uses (#1043, #1047)
CloudBurrow's: accepts and carries out DROP TABLE FUNCTION, which v0.3.1's analyzer refused ("Statement not supported: DropTableFunctionStatement") (#976, #986)

CloudBurrow's: keeps a FLOAT64 NaN, which SQLite made NULL when bound and when a function returned one, and parses and writes NaN and infinity literals, and an infinity inside an ARRAY or STRUCT (#1066, #1077)
CloudBurrow's: registers the unary minus operator, so -x of anything but a literal no longer fails "no such function: googlesqlite_unary_minus"

goccy/googlesqlite#80 (open upstream, by @cp-ant, unchanged but for its line numbers): builds a project's or dataset's sub-catalog without the builtin function set, which every catalog rebuild registered again into WebAssembly memory that only grows (#1057, #1017)
CloudBurrow's: addresses WebAssembly memory with unsigned 32-bit offsets, so a call past 2 GiB of engine heap no longer panics (#989)

CloudBurrow's: the module's own reproducible build of SQLite 3.53.1 (wasi-sdk 33, binaryen 129, wasm2go v0.4.3) with SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN 32767, so a table can have BigQuery's 10,000 columns; sqlite3.dat, binary, is replaced whole from a pinned file (#2008)

goCircl.notes: Cloud KMS post-quantum algorithms (#1946). Linked: third_party/circl-slhdsa is its sign/slhdsa (with internal/conv and internal/sha3), copied from this module's sources and given one constructor for a SHA-256 digest the client hashed (PROVENANCE.md): Go has no SLH-DSA, and Google's only Go one is internal to Tink, which the binary does not link. Test-only as a module: the compat suite's independent X-Wing encapsulation (kem/xwing) and HashSLH-DSA verification (sign/slhdsa). ML-DSA, ML-KEM and X-Wing on the server are Go's crypto/mldsa, crypto/mlkem, crypto/ecdh and crypto/sha3.

goKMS.notes: Generated contract types for the Cloud KMS implementation (#309), and the client the compatibility tests drive it with. Promoted from indirect (v1.32.0) to direct. The server's crypto is Go's standard library, but SLH-DSA, which is CIRCL's (goCircl, #1946; docs/upstream-evaluation.md, Cloud KMS amendment).

goMSSQL.notes: Cloud SQL for SQL Server (#1916): internal/service/sqladmin reaches a SQL Server instance's server as sa, to make its sqlserver user, databases, users and flags, as pgx and go-sql-driver/mysql reach PostgreSQL and MySQL. goCreackPty.notes: The console terminal (#781): internal/k8s starts `kubectl exec -it` on a pseudo-terminal, which kubectl requires before it allocates one in the container, as the session leader so a resize reaches it as SIGWINCH. golang.org/x/sys has no call that opens one.

goOpus.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's audio_track_extraction of an Opus track (#1739, internal/embedding/videoaudio.go): a pure Go Opus decoder (RFC 6716 / RFC 8251; CELT, SILK, hybrid; multistream mapping family 1), standard library only, no cgo and no unsafe in the packages linked (its libopus comparison harness is cgo behind the opusref build tag, not built here), go 1.24.11. #1811 replaced github.com/kazzmir/opus-go v1.7.0 with it: opus-go (libopus transpiled) kept uintptrs to goroutine-stack variables and grew its libc shim's pseudo-stack by copying (kazzmir/opus-go#79, unfixed on its master), so a stack that moved mid-decode corrupted the samples (0.76 of full scale from ffmpeg under -d=maymorestack=runtime.mayMoreStackMove), and -race needed checkptr off for it (#1808). This decoder is within 1.9e-7 of opus-go's samples on every test track and its 5.1 and 7.1 downmixes within 6e-5 of ffmpeg 9's libopus decode at 48 kHz, and gives identical samples with the stack moved at every function entry (TestDecodeOpusOnMovingStacks). Chosen over thesyncim/gopus and tphakala/go-opus (both need Go 1.27; CI builds with 1.26) and pion/opus (SILK only) (docs/upstream-evaluation.md).

gav1d.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's AV1 video (#1731, internal/embedding/video.go) and AVIF images (#1736, internal/embedding/avif.go), under the maintainer's approval of media decoder modules (2026-11-17): a pure Go port of dav1d with an AVIF reader, no cgo, no WebAssembly and no dependencies, 8 to 12 bits and every chroma format.
